passages.text: He who isolates himself pursues selfish desires; he rebels against all sound judgment.
passages.sermon:
A person who isolates himself acts alone.
He seeks only his own desires.
He does not care about others.
He rejects wise advice.
He opposes all sound judgment.
passages.original: לְֽ֭תַאֲוָה יְבַקֵּ֣שׁ נִפְרָ֑ד בְּכָל־ תּ֝וּשִׁיָּ֗ה יִתְגַּלָּֽע׃

passages.text: A fool does not delight in understanding, but only in airing his opinions.
passages.sermon:
A fool does not want understanding.
A fool does not seek wisdom.
A fool only wants to express his own thoughts.
A fool only wants to reveal what is in his heart.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ יַחְפֹּ֣ץ כְּ֭סִיל בִּתְבוּנָ֑ה כִּ֝֗י אִֽם־ בְּהִתְגַּלּ֥וֹת לִבּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: With a wicked man comes contempt as well, and shame is accompanied by disgrace.
passages.sermon:
A wicked man enters.
Contempt enters with him.
Shame arrives.
Disgrace comes with shame.
passages.original: בְּֽבוֹא־ רָ֭שָׁע בָּ֣א גַם־ בּ֑וּז וְֽעִם־ קָל֥וֹן חֶרְפָּֽה׃

passages.text: The words of a man’s mouth are deep waters; the fountain of wisdom is a bubbling brook.
passages.sermon:
A wise man speaks words that are deep.
His words are like deep waters.
Wisdom flows from him like a bubbling brook.
His wisdom is fresh and life-giving.
His words give understanding to others.
passages.original: מַ֣יִם עֲ֭מֻקִּים דִּבְרֵ֣י פִי־ אִ֑ישׁ נַ֥חַל נֹ֝בֵ֗עַ מְק֣וֹר חָכְמָֽה׃

passages.text: Showing partiality to the wicked is not good, nor is depriving the innocent of justice.
passages.sermon:
God calls us to be fair and just.
It is wrong to show favor to a wicked person.
It is also wrong to deny justice to an innocent person.
God wants us to treat everyone with fairness.
We must not let evil people receive special treatment.
We must not let good people lose their rights in court.
passages.original: שְׂאֵ֣ת פְּנֵי־ רָשָׁ֣ע לֹא־ ט֑וֹב לְהַטּ֥וֹת צַ֝דִּ֗יק בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃

passages.text: A fool’s lips bring him strife, and his mouth invites a beating.
passages.sermon:
A fool speaks with his lips.
His words cause arguments.
His mouth brings trouble to himself.
His mouth calls for a beating.
passages.original: שִׂפְתֵ֣י כְ֭סִיל יָבֹ֣אֽוּ בְרִ֑יב וּ֝פִ֗יו לְֽמַהֲלֻמ֥וֹת יִקְרָֽא׃

passages.text: A fool’s mouth is his ruin, and his lips are a snare to his soul.
passages.sermon:
A fool speaks with his mouth.
His mouth brings him ruin.
His lips trap his soul.
His words cause his own destruction.
His speech is a danger to himself.
passages.original: פִּֽי־ כְ֭סִיל מְחִתָּה־ ל֑וֹ וּ֝שְׂפָתָ֗יו מוֹקֵ֥שׁ נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

passages.text: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels that go down into the inmost being.
passages.sermon:
A gossip speaks words.
These words are like delicious food.
People listen to gossip eagerly.
The words of gossip go deep inside a person.
They reach the inmost part of a person’s heart.
passages.original: דִּבְרֵ֣י נִ֭רְגָּן כְּמִֽתְלַהֲמִ֑ים וְ֝הֵ֗ם יָרְד֥וּ חַדְרֵי־ בָֽטֶן׃

passages.text: Whoever is slothful in his work is brother to him who destroys.
passages.sermon:
A slothful person does not work hard.
A slothful person neglects his duties.
A slothful person is like a brother to a destroyer.
A destroyer brings harm.
A slothful person and a destroyer both cause loss.
passages.original: גַּ֭ם מִתְרַפֶּ֣ה בִמְלַאכְתּ֑וֹ אָ֥ח ה֝֗וּא לְבַ֣עַל מַשְׁחִֽית׃

passages.text: The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous run to it and are safe.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
His name is powerful.
His name is like a strong tower.
A righteous person trusts God.
The righteous run to God for help.
God keeps the righteous safe.
passages.original: מִגְדַּל־ עֹ֭ז שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה בּֽוֹ־ יָר֖וּץ צַדִּ֣יק וְנִשְׂגָּֽב׃

passages.text: A rich man’s wealth is his fortified city; it is like a high wall in his imagination.
passages.sermon:
A rich man trusts his wealth.
His wealth is like a strong city to him.
He thinks his wealth protects him.
He imagines his wealth is a high wall.
He believes his wealth keeps him safe.
passages.original: ה֣וֹן עָ֭שִׁיר קִרְיַ֣ת עֻזּ֑וֹ וּכְחוֹמָ֥ה נִ֝שְׂגָּבָ֗ה בְּמַשְׂכִּיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Before his downfall a man’s heart is proud, but humility comes before honor.
passages.sermon:
A man’s heart becomes proud before his downfall.
Pride comes before destruction.
Humility comes before honor.
Honor follows humility.
passages.original: לִפְנֵי־ שֶׁ֭בֶר יִגְבַּ֣הּ לֵב־ אִ֑ישׁ וְלִפְנֵ֖י כָב֣וֹד עֲנָוָֽה׃

passages.text: He who answers a matter before he hears it— this is folly and disgrace to him.
passages.sermon: A person may answer a question before he listens to it.\r\nThis person acts foolishly.\r\nThis person brings shame on himself.
passages.original: מֵשִׁ֣יב דָּ֭בָר בְּטֶ֣רֶם יִשְׁמָ֑ע אִוֶּ֥לֶת הִיא־ ל֝֗וֹ וּכְלִמָּֽה׃

passages.text: The spirit of a man can endure his sickness, but who can survive a broken spirit?
passages.sermon:
A man has a spirit inside him.
This spirit helps him endure sickness.
A strong spirit gives him strength to face illness.
But a broken spirit is different.
No one can carry a broken spirit.
No one can survive when his spirit is crushed.
passages.original: רֽוּחַ־ אִ֭ישׁ יְכַלְכֵּ֣ל מַחֲלֵ֑הוּ וְר֥וּחַ נְ֝כֵאָ֗ה מִ֣י יִשָּׂאֶֽנָּה׃

passages.text: The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks it out.
passages.sermon:
A discerning person has understanding.
A discerning person gains knowledge.
A wise person listens carefully.
A wise person seeks knowledge.
passages.original: לֵ֣ב נָ֭בוֹן יִקְנֶה־ דָּ֑עַת וְאֹ֥זֶן חֲ֝כָמִ֗ים תְּבַקֶּשׁ־ דָּֽעַת׃

passages.text: A man’s gift opens doors for him, and brings him before great men.
passages.sermon:
A man can give a gift.
This gift makes room for him.
The gift opens new opportunities for the man.
The gift brings the man before important people.
The man stands before great leaders because of his gift.
passages.original: מַתָּ֣ן אָ֭דָם יַרְחִ֣יב ל֑וֹ וְלִפְנֵ֖י גְדֹלִ֣ים יַנְחֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: The first to state his case seems right until another comes and cross-examines him.
passages.sermon:
A righteous person speaks first in a dispute.
He appears correct at first.
Then another person comes.
The second person examines the first person's words.
The second person questions and investigates the case.
passages.original: צַדִּ֣יק הָרִאשׁ֣וֹן בְּרִיב֑וֹ יָבֹא רֵ֝עֵ֗הוּ וַחֲקָרֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Casting the lot ends quarrels and separates strong opponents.
passages.sermon:
Casting lots can end quarrels.
Casting lots can separate strong opponents.
Casting lots is a way to settle disputes.
Strong opponents may not agree.
Casting lots can divide them and bring peace.
passages.original: מִ֭דְיָנִים יַשְׁבִּ֣ית הַגּוֹרָ֑ל וּבֵ֖ין עֲצוּמִ֣ים יַפְרִֽיד׃

passages.text: An offended brother is harder to win than a fortified city, and disputes are like the bars of a castle.
passages.sermon:
An offended brother is very hard to win back.
He is harder to win than a strong, fortified city.
Disputes separate people.
Disputes are like the bars of a castle.
The bars of a castle keep people apart and make entry difficult.
passages.original: אָ֗ח נִפְשָׁ֥ע מִקִּרְיַת־ עֹ֑ז וּמְדוֹנִים כִּבְרִ֥יחַ אַרְמֽוֹן׃

passages.text: From the fruit of his mouth a man’s belly is filled; with the harvest from his lips he is satisfied.
passages.sermon:
A man speaks words.
His words are like fruit.
These words fill his belly.
His lips produce a harvest.
He is satisfied by what his lips produce.
passages.original: מִפְּרִ֣י פִי־ אִ֭ישׁ תִּשְׂבַּ֣ע בִּטְנ֑וֹ תְּבוּאַ֖ת שְׂפָתָ֣יו יִשְׂבָּֽע׃

passages.text: Life and death are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
passages.sermon:
The tongue has great power.
It holds the power of life.
It holds the power of death.
People who love to speak will eat the fruit of their words.
Their words will bring results.
These results can be good or bad.
passages.original: מָ֣וֶת וְ֭חַיִּים בְּיַד־ לָשׁ֑וֹן וְ֝אֹהֲבֶ֗יהָ יֹאכַ֥ל פִּרְיָֽהּ׃

passages.text: He who finds a wife finds a good thing and obtains favor from the LORD.
passages.sermon: A man who finds a wife finds something good.\r\nHe receives favor from the LORD.
passages.original: מָצָ֣א אִ֭שָּׁה מָ֣צָא ט֑וֹב וַיָּ֥פֶק רָ֝צ֗וֹן מֵיְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: The poor man pleads for mercy, but the rich man answers harshly.
passages.sermon: A poor man speaks with pleas for mercy.\r\nA rich man answers with harsh words.
passages.original: תַּחֲנוּנִ֥ים יְדַבֶּר־ רָ֑שׁ וְ֝עָשִׁ֗יר יַעֲנֶ֥ה עַזּֽוֹת׃

passages.text: A man of many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who stays closer than a brother.
passages.sermon:
A man can have many companions.
He may still come to ruin.
There is a friend who stays close.
This friend is closer than a brother.
passages.original: אִ֣ישׁ רֵ֭עִים לְהִתְרֹעֵ֑עַ וְיֵ֥שׁ אֹ֝הֵ֗ב דָּבֵ֥ק מֵאָֽח׃
